questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates proficiency in partition DP with non-additive segment scores (bitwise AND). It assesses understanding of precomputation strategies and solution reconstruction.

## Key Concepts
- DP for partitioning an array into k contiguous blocks
- Precomputing subarray AND values in O(n²) time
- Backtracking to reconstruct segment endpoints
- Time/space trade-offs

## Code Example
```python
def max_and_partition(A, k):
    n = len(A)
    andv = [[0] * n for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        andv[i][i] = A[i]
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            andv[i][j] = andv[i][j-1] & A[j]
    
    dp = [[-float('inf')] * (k + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        dp[i][1] = andv[0][i-1]
    
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for t in range(2, min(k, i) + 1):
            for p in range(t - 1, i):
                dp[i][t] = max(dp[i][t], dp[p][t-1] + andv[p][i-1])
    
    return dp[n][k]
```

## Why This Is Asked
Design a DP that handles partitioning with a per-element penalty, enabling exact k blocks with reconstruction; this variant extends standard partition DP by a linear per-element cost and a prefix-sum transform.

## Key Concepts
- DP over fixed-k partitions
- Prefix sums with a constant penalty transform
- Running bestPrev to achieve O(nk) time
- Traceback pointers for block endpoints

## Code Example
```javascript
const n = A.length;
const S = new Array(n+1).fill(0);
for (let i=1; i<=n; i++) S[i] = S[i-1] + A[i-1];
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to extend to at most k blocks or include negative penalties?
- Can you optimize space to O(n) per k without losing reconstruction?
